paragraphs.text: And he began to speak unto them in parables. A man planted a vineyard, and set a hedge about it, and digged a pit for the winepress, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into another country.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖν· Ἀμπελῶνα ἄνθρωπος ἐφύτευσεν, καὶ περιέθηκεν φραγμὸν καὶ ὤρυξεν ὑπολήνιον καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν πύργον, καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ērxato autois en parabolais lalein· Ampelōna anthrōpos ephyteusen, kai periethēken phragmon kai ōryxen hypolēnion kai ōkodomēsen pyrgon, kai exedeto auton geōrgois, kai apedēmēsen.

paragraphs.text: And at the season he sent to the husbandmen a servant, that he might receive from the husbandmen of the fruits of the vineyard.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς τῷ καιρῷ δοῦλον, ἵνα παρὰ τῶν γεωργῶν λάβῃ ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος·
paragraphs.translit: kai apesteilen pros tous geōrgous tō kairō doulon, hina para tōn geōrgōn labē apo tōn karpōn tou ampelōnos·

paragraphs.text: And they took him, and beat him, and sent him away empty.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λαβόντες αὐτὸν ἔδειραν καὶ ἀπέστειλαν κενόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai labontes auton edeiran kai apesteilan kenon.

paragraphs.text: And again he sent unto them another servant; and him they wounded in the head, and handled shamefully.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἄλλον δοῦλον· κἀκεῖνον ἐκεφαλίωσαν καὶ ἠτίμασαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai palin apesteilen pros autous allon doulon· kakeinon ekephaliōsan kai ētimasan.

paragraphs.text: And he sent another; and him they killed: and many others; beating some, and killing some.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἄλλον ἀπέστειλεν· κἀκεῖνον ἀπέκτειναν, καὶ πολλοὺς ἄλλους, οὓς μὲν δέροντες οὓς δὲ ἀποκτέννοντες.
paragraphs.translit: kai allon apesteilen· kakeinon apekteinan, kai pollous allous, hous men derontes hous de apoktennontes.

paragraphs.text: He had yet one, a beloved son: he sent him last unto them, saying, They will reverence my son.
paragraphs.original: ἔτι ἕνα εἶχεν, υἱὸν ἀγαπητόν· ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν ἔσχατον πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων ὅτι Ἐντραπήσονται τὸν υἱόν μου.
paragraphs.translit: eti hena eichen, hyion agapēton· apesteilen auton eschaton pros autous legōn hoti Entrapēsontai ton hyion mou.

paragraphs.text: But those husbandmen said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance shall be ours.
paragraphs.original: ἐκεῖνοι δὲ οἱ γεωργοὶ πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς εἶπαν ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος· δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἡμῶν ἔσται ἡ κληρονομία.
paragraphs.translit: ekeinoi de hoi geōrgoi pros heautous eipan hoti Houtos estin ho klēronomos· deute apokteinōmen auton, kai hēmōn estai hē klēronomia.

paragraphs.text: And they took him, and killed him, and cast him forth out of the vineyard.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λαβόντες ἀπέκτειναν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος.
paragraphs.translit: kai labontes apekteinan auton, kai exebalon auton exō tou ampelōnos.

paragraphs.text: What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.
paragraphs.original: τί ποιήσει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος; ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀπολέσει τοὺς γεωργούς, καὶ δώσει τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἄλλοις.
paragraphs.translit: ti poiēsei ho kyrios tou ampelōnos; eleusetai kai apolesei tous geōrgous, kai dōsei ton ampelōna allois.

paragraphs.text: Have ye not read even this scripture: The stone which the builders rejected, The same was made the head of the corner;
paragraphs.original: οὐδὲ τὴν γραφὴν ταύτην ἀνέγνωτε· Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες, οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας·
paragraphs.translit: oude tēn graphēn tautēn anegnōte· Lithon hon apedokimasan hoi oikodomountes, houtos egenēthē eis kephalēn gōnias·

paragraphs.text: This was from the Lord, And it is marvellous in our eyes?
paragraphs.original: παρὰ κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη, καὶ ἔστιν θαυμαστὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν;
paragraphs.translit: para kyriou egeneto hautē, kai estin thaumastē en ophthalmois hēmōn;

paragraphs.text: And they sought to lay hold on him; and they feared the multitude; for they perceived that he spake the parable against them: and they left him, and went away.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸν ὄχλον, ἔγνωσαν γὰρ ὅτι πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν εἶπεν. καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθον.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ezētoun auton kratēsai, kai ephobēthēsan ton ochlon, egnōsan gar hoti pros autous tēn parabolēn eipen. kai aphentes auton apēlthon.

paragraphs.text: And they send unto him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, that they might catch him in talk.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν πρὸς αὐτόν τινας τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν ἵνα αὐτὸν ἀγρεύσωσιν λόγῳ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai apostellousin pros auton tinas tōn Pharisaiōn kai tōn Hērōdianōn hina auton agreusōsin logō.

paragraphs.text: And when they were come, they say unto him, Teacher, we know that thou art true, and carest not for any one; for thou regardest not the person of men, but of a truth teachest the way of God: Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐλθόντες λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός, οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων, ἀλλʼ ἐπʼ ἀληθείας τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ διδάσκεις· ἔξεστιν δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι ἢ οὔ; δῶμεν ἢ μὴ δῶμεν;
paragraphs.translit: kai elthontes legousin autō· Didaskale, oidamen hoti alēthēs ei kai ou melei soi peri oudenos, ou gar blepeis eis prosōpon anthrōpōn, allʼ epʼ alētheias tēn hodon tou theou didaskeis· exestin dounai kēnson Kaisari ē ou; dōmen ē mē dōmen;

paragraphs.text: Shall we give, or shall we not give? But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said unto them, Why make ye trial of me? bring me a denarius, that I may see it.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὴν ὑπόκρισιν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί με πειράζετε; φέρετέ μοι δηνάριον ἵνα ἴδω.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eidōs autōn tēn hypokrisin eipen autois· Ti me peirazete; pherete moi dēnarion hina idō.

paragraphs.text: And they brought it. And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? And they said unto him, Caesar`s.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἤνεγκαν. καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Καίσαρος.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de ēnenkan. kai legei autois· Tinos hē eikōn hautē kai hē epigraphē; hoi de eipan autō· Kaisaros.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto them, Render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar`s, and unto God the things that are God`s. And they marvelled greatly at him.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τὰ Καίσαρος ἀπόδοτε Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ. καὶ ἐξεθαύμαζον ἐπʼ αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous eipen autois· Ta Kaisaros apodote Kaisari kai ta tou theou tō theō. kai exethaumazon epʼ autō.

paragraphs.text: And there come unto him Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection; and they asked him, saying,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται Σαδδουκαῖοι πρὸς αὐτόν, οἵτινες λέγουσιν ἀνάστασιν μὴ εἶναι, καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες·
paragraphs.translit: Kai erchontai Saddoukaioi pros auton, hoitines legousin anastasin mē einai, kai epērōtōn auton legontes·

paragraphs.text: Teacher, Moses wrote unto us, If a man`s brother die, and leave a wife behind him, and leave no child, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
paragraphs.original: Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς ἔγραψεν ἡμῖν ὅτι ἐάν τινος ἀδελφὸς ἀποθάνῃ καὶ καταλίπῃ γυναῖκα καὶ μὴ ἀφῇ τέκνον, ἵνα λάβῃ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ ἐξαναστήσῃ σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Didaskale, Mōysēs egrapsen hēmin hoti ean tinos adelphos apothanē kai katalipē gynaika kai mē aphē teknon, hina labē ho adelphos autou tēn gynaika kai exanastēsē sperma tō adelphō autou.

paragraphs.text: There were seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and dying left no seed;
paragraphs.original: ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοὶ ἦσαν· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος ἔλαβεν γυναῖκα, καὶ ἀποθνῄσκων οὐκ ἀφῆκεν σπέρμα·
paragraphs.translit: hepta adelphoi ēsan· kai ho prōtos elaben gynaika, kai apothnēskōn ouk aphēken sperma·

paragraphs.text: and the second took her, and died, leaving no seed behind him; and the third likewise:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἔλαβεν αὐτήν, καὶ ἀπέθανεν μὴ καταλιπὼν σπέρμα, καὶ ὁ τρίτος ὡσαύτως·
paragraphs.translit: kai ho deuteros elaben autēn, kai apethanen mē katalipōn sperma, kai ho tritos hōsautōs·

paragraphs.text: and the seven left no seed. Last of all the woman also died.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ οὐκ ἀφῆκαν σπέρμα· ἔσχατον πάντων καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἀπέθανεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi hepta ouk aphēkan sperma· eschaton pantōn kai hē gynē apethanen.

paragraphs.text: In the resurrection whose wife shall she be of them? for the seven had her to wife.
paragraphs.original: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ὅταν ἀναστῶσιν τίνος αὐτῶν ἔσται γυνή; οἱ γὰρ ἑπτὰ ἔσχον αὐτὴν γυναῖκα.
paragraphs.translit: en tē anastasei hotan anastōsin tinos autōn estai gynē; hoi gar hepta eschon autēn gynaika.

paragraphs.text: Jesus said unto them, Is it not for this cause that ye err, that ye know not the scriptures, nor the power of God?
paragraphs.original: ἔφη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐ διὰ τοῦτο πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ θεοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: ephē autois ho Iēsous· Ou dia touto planasthe mē eidotes tas graphas mēde tēn dynamin tou theou;

paragraphs.text: For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage; but are as angels in heaven.
paragraphs.original: ὅταν γὰρ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῶσιν, οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται, ἀλλʼ εἰσὶν ὡς ἄγγελοι ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς·
paragraphs.translit: hotan gar ek nekrōn anastōsin, oute gamousin oute gamizontai, allʼ eisin hōs angeloi en tois ouranois·

paragraphs.text: But as touching the dead, that they are raised; have ye not read in the book of Moses, in [the place concerning] the Bush, how God spake unto him, saying, I [am] the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?
paragraphs.original: περὶ δὲ τῶν νεκρῶν ὅτι ἐγείρονται οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ἐν τῇ βίβλῳ Μωϋσέως ἐπὶ τοῦ βάτου πῶς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς λέγων· Ἐγὼ ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακώβ;
paragraphs.translit: peri de tōn nekrōn hoti egeirontai ouk anegnōte en tē biblō Mōyseōs epi tou batou pōs eipen autō ho theos legōn· Egō ho theos Abraam kai ho theos Isaak kai ho theos Iakōb;

paragraphs.text: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living: ye do greatly err.
paragraphs.original: οὐκ ἔστιν θεὸς νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων· πολὺ πλανᾶσθε.
paragraphs.translit: ouk estin theos nekrōn alla zōntōn· poly planasthe.

paragraphs.text: And one of the scribes came, and heard them questioning together, and knowing that he had answered them well, asked him, What commandment is the first of all?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ προσελθὼν εἷς τῶν γραμματέων ἀκούσας αὐτῶν συζητούντων, ἰδὼν ὅτι καλῶς ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς, ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτόν· Ποία ἐστὶν ἐντολὴ πρώτη πάντων;
paragraphs.translit: Kai proselthōn heis tōn grammateōn akousas autōn syzētountōn, idōn hoti kalōs apekrithē autois, epērōtēsen auton· Poia estin entolē prōtē pantōn;

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered, The first is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God, the Lord is one:
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Πρώτη ἐστίν· Ἄκουε, Ἰσραήλ, κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν κύριος εἷς ἐστιν,
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē ho Iēsous hoti Prōtē estin· Akoue, Israēl, kyrios ho theos hēmōn kyrios heis estin,

paragraphs.text: and thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ψυχῆς σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς διανοίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος σου.
paragraphs.translit: kai agapēseis kyrion ton theon sou ex holēs tēs kardias sou kai ex holēs tēs psychēs sou kai ex holēs tēs dianoias sou kai ex holēs tēs ischyos sou.

paragraphs.text: The second is this, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.
paragraphs.original: δευτέρα αὕτη· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν. μείζων τούτων ἄλλη ἐντολὴ οὐκ ἔστιν.
paragraphs.translit: deutera hautē· Agapēseis ton plēsion sou hōs seauton. meizōn toutōn allē entolē ouk estin.

paragraphs.text: And the scribe said unto him, Of a truth, Teacher, thou hast well said that he is one; and there is none other but he:
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ γραμματεύς· Καλῶς, διδάσκαλε, ἐπʼ ἀληθείας εἶπες ὅτι εἷς ἐστιν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἄλλος πλὴν αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autō ho grammateus· Kalōs, didaskale, epʼ alētheias eipes hoti heis estin kai ouk estin allos plēn autou·

paragraphs.text: and to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is much more than all whole burnt-offerings and sacrifices.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὸ ἀγαπᾶν αὐτὸν ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς συνέσεως καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος καὶ τὸ ἀγαπᾶν τὸν πλησίον ὡς ἑαυτὸν περισσότερόν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων καὶ θυσιῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai to agapan auton ex holēs tēs kardias kai ex holēs tēs syneseōs kai ex holēs tēs ischyos kai to agapan ton plēsion hōs heauton perissoteron estin pantōn tōn holokautōmatōn kai thysiōn.

paragraphs.text: And when Jesus saw that he answered discreetly, he said unto him, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God. And no man after that durst ask him any question.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ὅτι νουνεχῶς ἀπεκρίθη εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Οὐ μακρὰν εἶ ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ. καὶ οὐδεὶς οὐκέτι ἐτόλμα αὐτὸν ἐπερωτῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho Iēsous idōn auton hoti nounechōs apekrithē eipen autō· Ou makran ei apo tēs basileias tou theou. kai oudeis ouketi etolma auton eperōtēsai.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus answered and said, as he taught in the temple, How say the scribes that the Christ is the son of David?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν διδάσκων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ· Πῶς λέγουσιν οἱ γραμματεῖς ὅτι ὁ χριστὸς υἱὸς Δαυίδ ἐστιν;
paragraphs.translit: Kai apokritheis ho Iēsous elegen didaskōn en tō hierō· Pōs legousin hoi grammateis hoti ho christos hyios Dauid estin;

paragraphs.text: David himself said in the Holy Spirit, The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, Till I make thine enemies the footstool of thy feet.
paragraphs.original: αὐτὸς Δαυὶδ εἶπεν ἐν τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ· Εἶπεν κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου.
paragraphs.translit: autos Dauid eipen en tō pneumati tō hagiō· Eipen kyrios tō kyriō mou· Kathou ek dexiōn mou heōs an thō tous echthrous sou hypokatō tōn podōn sou.

paragraphs.text: David himself calleth him Lord; and whence is he his son? And the common people heard him gladly.
paragraphs.original: αὐτὸς Δαυὶδ λέγει αὐτὸν κύριον, καὶ πόθεν αὐτοῦ ἐστιν υἱός; καὶ ὁ πολὺς ὄχλος ἤκουεν αὐτοῦ ἡδέως.
paragraphs.translit: autos Dauid legei auton kyrion, kai pothen autou estin hyios; kai ho polys ochlos ēkouen autou hēdeōs.

paragraphs.text: And in his teaching he said, Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk in long robes, and [to have] salutations in the marketplaces,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν· Βλέπετε ἀπὸ τῶν γραμματέων τῶν θελόντων ἐν στολαῖς περιπατεῖν καὶ ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς
paragraphs.translit: Kai en tē didachē autou elegen· Blepete apo tōn grammateōn tōn thelontōn en stolais peripatein kai aspasmous en tais agorais

paragraphs.text: and chief seats in the synagogues, and chief places at feasts:
paragraphs.original: καὶ πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ πρωτοκλισίας ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις,
paragraphs.translit: kai prōtokathedrias en tais synagōgais kai prōtoklisias en tois deipnois,

paragraphs.text: they that devour widows` houses, and for a pretence make long prayers; these shall receive greater condemnation.
paragraphs.original: οἱ κατεσθίοντες τὰς οἰκίας τῶν χηρῶν καὶ προφάσει μακρὰ προσευχόμενοι· οὗτοι λήμψονται περισσότερον κρίμα.
paragraphs.translit: hoi katesthiontes tas oikias tōn chērōn kai prophasei makra proseuchomenoi· houtoi lēmpsontai perissoteron krima.

paragraphs.text: And he sat down over against the treasury, and beheld how the multitude cast money into the treasury: and many that were rich cast in much.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ καθίσας κατέναντι τοῦ γαζοφυλακίου ἐθεώρει πῶς ὁ ὄχλος βάλλει χαλκὸν εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον· καὶ πολλοὶ πλούσιοι ἔβαλλον πολλά·
paragraphs.translit: Kai kathisas katenanti tou gazophylakiou etheōrei pōs ho ochlos ballei chalkon eis to gazophylakion· kai polloi plousioi eballon polla·

paragraphs.text: And there came a poor widow, and she cast in two mites, which make a farthing.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐλθοῦσα μία χήρα πτωχὴ ἔβαλεν λεπτὰ δύο, ὅ ἐστιν κοδράντης.
paragraphs.translit: kai elthousa mia chēra ptōchē ebalen lepta dyo, ho estin kodrantēs.

paragraphs.text: And he called unto him his disciples, and said unto them, Verily I say unto you, This poor widow cast in more than all they that are casting into the treasury:
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα αὕτη ἡ πτωχὴ πλεῖον πάντων ἔβαλεν τῶν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον·
paragraphs.translit: kai proskalesamenos tous mathētas autou eipen autois· Amēn legō hymin hoti hē chēra hautē hē ptōchē pleion pantōn ebalen tōn ballontōn eis to gazophylakion·

paragraphs.text: for they all did cast in of their superfluity; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, [even] all her living.
paragraphs.original: πάντες γὰρ ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος αὐτοῖς ἔβαλον, αὕτη δὲ ἐκ τῆς ὑστερήσεως αὐτῆς πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν ἔβαλεν, ὅλον τὸν βίον αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: pantes gar ek tou perisseuontos autois ebalon, hautē de ek tēs hysterēseōs autēs panta hosa eichen ebalen, holon ton bion autēs.
